title: A cast mineral solid that can be a complete primary structure

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a mineral material that can be cast into primary structural members and itself provide the tensile strength, ductile deformation and resistance after cracking needed to carry design loads. It would also retain useful structural capacity after a specified fire exposure and be economical enough to make reinforcing bars optional in qualifying applications. The ambition combines material behavior, full-size member performance and construction economics; none of those properties alone would establish completion.

A central distinction remains to be settled: an intrinsically ductile mineral solid is different from a mineral composite whose deformation capacity comes from fibers bridging cracks. Both could potentially serve the broader goal of structural self-sufficiency, but a successful mineral-fiber composite would not by itself demonstrate intrinsic ductility of its matrix. Here, an unreinforced member means one without reinforcing bars or an equivalent separate reinforcing system; whether dispersed mineral fibers are permitted remains an explicit scope question.

significance.text: Conditional engineering synthesis: if the material met the combined structural, fire and economic requirements, ordinary members within its demonstrated design envelope could be cast without installing reinforcing bars. Where embedded steel reinforcement was eliminated, corrosion of that reinforcement would cease to be a deterioration mechanism, and its fabrication and placement work would be removed. These are consequences of actually displacing reinforcement, rather than benefits established by a strong or ductile laboratory specimen alone.

The supplied research attributes a cost disadvantage relative to conventional concrete to a June 2024 review of ECC strengthening. If that report is confirmed in context, it illustrates why the proposed innovation must succeed economically as well as mechanically. However, a reported cost disadvantage does not establish that fiber cost alone causes limited adoption, or that existing ductile cementitious composites are confined to repair and specialty members.

Conditional downstream possibilities include simpler reinforcement logistics, different member geometries and revised seismic detailing. Equivalent seismic performance would still require validation of cyclic behavior, connections and the complete structural system. Removing steel would not establish overall durability, and a material that survives fire would not automatically make an entire building fire resilient. Foundations, connections, stability, deflection, other deterioration mechanisms and economical construction would remain constraints. The supplied evidence does not establish the earlier claim that steel supplies much of reinforced concrete’s residual capacity after fire.

missing_breakthrough.text: The research target is a combination of sufficient structural tension capacity, stable deformation after cracking, useful capacity after fire and competitive installed cost in a cast mineral material. The supplied record does not establish that this combination has been achieved, but it also cannot establish its absence across the field through November 1, 2026. The unresolved capability should therefore be understood as the proposed target, rather than a verified exhaustive statement about every existing material.

Engineering synthesis: the material must sustain load as cracks initiate and develop, without allowing deformation to concentrate prematurely into a single unstable fracture. If intrinsic ductility is claimed, the mineral matrix must provide the relevant deformation mechanism independently of fiber bridging. If mineral fibers are allowed, the challenge instead includes producing reliable bridging and load transfer while controlling fiber distribution, interfaces and processing. Distributed cracking is useful evidence of deformation capacity, but it does not identify which of these mechanisms supplies it.

Engineering synthesis: fire performance requires more than replacing a polymer fiber with a heat-resistant constituent. The material must retain a usable load path through the specified heating, loading and cooling history, including the effects of cracking and possible spalling. The supplied research reports elevated-temperature strength loss and spalling in one high-strength polyethylene-fiber ECC study, but the available review cannot verify its experimental conditions or generalize those findings to every polymer-fiber composite.

Engineering synthesis: scaling from a tensile coupon to a primary member introduces variability, casting defects, curing differences and interactions among tension, compression, shear and restraint. A practical material would also need dependable long-term deformation and durability, buildable connections and repeatable production. Its economic challenge is to compete at the level of an installed structural solution, including required material volume, processing, curing and placement, rather than merely matching a price per unit volume.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes tensile strain capacities of 3%–12%, tensile strengths above 3 MPa and fiber volumes generally below 2% to the 2023 review “Structural application of engineered cementitious composites (ECC): A state-of-the-art review.” Those reported values describe substantial tensile deformation in fiber-containing cementitious composites; they would not establish intrinsic mineral-matrix ductility or bar-free performance of full-size members. Access was described as abstract-level, with the numerical passage returned in a search record. The validated review had no saved article artifact or inspected document text with which to check the values, their scope or whether the bounds apply to the same formulations.

The June 2024 review “Engineered cementitious composite (ECC) strengthening of reinforced concrete structures: A state-of-the-art review” is reported in the supplied research to identify higher cost than conventional concrete as a constraint on large-scale industrial adoption. This is a reported review conclusion, not a quantified installed-cost comparison for a complete replacement structure. The research had abstract-level access and a passage returned with a search record; no saved source artifact was available to the validated review. The author list and DOI were not retrieved, which does not imply that they are absent from the publication.

The supplied research describes the July 2025 paper “Use of polypropylene fibers to mitigate spalling in high strength PE-ECC under elevated temperature” as an open paper whose retrieved conclusions reported a significant decrease in compressive strength after exposure above 400°C and severe spalling in a polyethylene-only high-strength ECC during rapid heating to 600°C. The earlier candidate called the spalling explosive; that stronger characterization cannot be confirmed from the supplied review. These are attributed findings for the studied materials and exposure conditions. Compressive-strength loss and spalling do not directly quantify retained tensile ductility, and the results do not establish a universal failure temperature for polymer-fiber composites.

Although conclusions were described as retrieved for the 2025 paper, the validated review had no saved article artifact or inspected document text to verify the heating protocol, specimen conditions, cooling procedure, strength measurements or effectiveness of the polypropylene addition named in the title. Its authors were not extracted. The title alone cannot establish that the proposed spalling mitigation succeeded or preserved structural capacity.

Taken together, the supplied accounts describe relevant partial capabilities and limitations, without establishing the complete proposed innovation. The asserted comparison with steel-fiber ultra-high-performance concrete—specialty use and much smaller tensile strain—cannot be substantiated from these records. Neither can a field-wide conclusion about the continuing necessity of reinforcing bars. The dated reports concern 2023–2025; no freshness evidence establishes developments through November 1, 2026. These access and coverage limits leave questions open rather than proving the reported results false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: cast a bar-free mineral member at a stated building or bridge scale and demonstrate a stable design flexural or tensile mechanism, controlled distributed cracking and useful deformation capacity. Specify a ductile reinforced-member comparator and test under comparable loading, restraint and performance requirements. Define acceptance thresholds before testing. Coupon strain of several percent or fiber-bridging stress of a few megapascals would be relevant material evidence, but would not alone establish that the member can replace the comparator.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed mechanism test: state whether dispersed mineral fibers are allowed. If intrinsic matrix ductility is part of the claim, demonstrate that mechanism separately from fiber bridging or other distributed reinforcement. If the successful material instead relies on mineral fibers, describe it as a composite and assess it against the broader structural goal without treating that result as proof of intrinsic matrix ductility.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed mechanism test

completion_criteria.text: Proposed fire demonstration: specify the fire curve, duration, applied load, restraint, cooling procedure and minimum acceptable capacity during exposure and after cooling. Establish what fraction of the pre-exposure capacity must remain and why it is adequate for the intended application. Where the comparison concerns loss of polymer-fiber ductility, verify that the same exposure depletes the relevant mechanism in an appropriate comparison material. A temperature high enough to melt a fiber is not, by itself, a complete structural fire test.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed fire demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical demonstration: compare installed structural cost with ordinary reinforced concrete for an equivalent function, including member dimensions, material volume, processing, curing, placement, connections and any reinforcement still required elsewhere. Evaluate the loading modes, cyclic behavior where relevant, long-term deformation, durability and construction tolerances needed for the claimed applications. The earlier ambition of ordinary-concrete-like material pricing remains useful, but installed cost is the more direct test of economical substitution.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed practical demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirement: repeat the material and member results across independent batches, representative casting conditions and independent testing, and report variability and failure modes. Establish a bounded design envelope identifying the applications, dimensions, exposures and loading histories actually supported. These are proposed criteria, not established consensus thresholds. Even a broad successful test program would demonstrate performance within that envelope, rather than literal universality across all buildings, bridges or fires.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility requirement

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: STR-01, “Flaw-tolerant bulk members at near-theoretical specific strength,” shares the ambition of changing what a structural material can carry. STR-03 instead centers on castability, structural tension, deformation capacity, fire performance and economical independence from reinforcing bars. Near-theoretical strength relative to weight would not itself establish those properties.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-02, “Repeated autonomous restoration of full structural capacity,” and STR-06, “Load-bearing structures that grow and remodel,” concern restoration or adaptation over time. STR-03 could overlap with either if its material also healed or remodeled, but neither function is required by this concept. STR-09, “A prospectively validated law of structural lifespan,” concerns predicting service life; it could help establish confidence in STR-03’s durability without supplying its load-bearing mechanism.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-04, “Field-scale broadband seismic cloaking,” STR-10, “Ordinary buildings that remain undamaged and usable after design-level earthquakes,” and STR-11, “Passive damping that removes resonant amplification from governing modes,” concern earthquake exposure, system outcomes or dynamic response. STR-03’s proposed ductility could contribute to seismic performance, but would not itself demonstrate cloaking, elimination of resonant amplification or undamaged post-earthquake usability. Controlled cracking sufficient for ductility may still leave damage.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-05, “Primary members whose mechanical state can be reprogrammed in service,” and STR-08, “Primary structure that stores the host system’s useful energy,” add distinct operational functions to load-bearing structure. A STR-03 material might eventually support those functions, but reprogrammability and energy storage are not requirements for economical structural self-sufficiency.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-07, “Topological control that denies an undesigned collapse mechanism,” concerns the availability of structural failure paths. STR-12, “Disproportionate collapse made unavailable after loss of any one primary member,” concerns system robustness after member loss. STR-03’s material behavior could contribute to either, but tensile ductility does not alone establish alternate load paths or prevent disproportionate collapse. The earlier description of STR-07 as lattice-directed cracking is narrower than its supplied title supports. These comparisons are provisional because the roster supplies titles rather than complete concept descriptions.

change_log.change: Preserved STR-03’s identity and integrated its mechanical, fire, scale and economic ambitions into a single conditional concept.
change_log.reason: The combined target remains coherent even though the supplied evidence does not establish its achievement or field-wide absence.

change_log.change: Distinguished intrinsic mineral-matrix ductility from deformation produced by dispersed mineral-fiber bridging.
change_log.reason: Distributed cracking and composite tensile strain do not independently establish intrinsic matrix ductility.

change_log.change: Retained the reported ECC strain, strength, fiber-volume and temperature figures with source-specific attribution and access limitations.
change_log.reason: The figures are useful research detail, but the validated review lacked saved artifacts or inspected article text to verify their context.

change_log.change: Qualified the 2025 fire findings as formulation- and protocol-specific reports, and used severe rather than confirmed explosive spalling.
change_log.reason: The supplied account supports the narrower wording; compressive-strength loss and spalling also do not directly measure retained tensile ductility.

change_log.change: Removed categorical claims about fiber costs causing specialty-only adoption, UHPC strain comparisons and steel’s contribution to residual fire capacity.
change_log.reason: Those generalizations exceed the evidence available in the supplied review.

change_log.change: Limited direct benefits to qualifying members that actually displace reinforcement and separated them from conditional system-level possibilities.
change_log.reason: Eliminating reinforcement removes its corrosion mechanism and placement work, but does not establish overall durability, seismic equivalence or quantified labor savings.

change_log.change: Expanded completion proposals to specify structural comparators, fire protocols, mechanism identification, reproducibility and installed cost.
change_log.reason: These make the ambition testable while preserving the distinction between proposed criteria and accepted standards.

change_log.change: Explained relationships with every other supplied roster entry and corrected the narrow characterization of STR-07.
change_log.reason: The supplied STR-07 title concerns collapse mechanisms more broadly than lattice-directed cracking, and title-only comparisons must remain provisional.

unresolved_issues: Whether dispersed mineral fibers are permitted, and whether intrinsic matrix ductility is mandatory or a preferred route to the broader structural goal.

The source texts and experimental context needed to verify the reported ECC ranges, cost conclusion and elevated-temperature findings; all three indexed sources lack saved artifacts in the supplied review.
Whether the 2023 strain, strength and fiber-volume bounds describe the same formulations or a range across different ECC systems.
The 2025 study’s heating, loading and cooling conditions, spalling characterization, tensile behavior after exposure and measured effectiveness of polypropylene additions.
The appropriate member comparator, deformation requirement, fire-retention threshold and installed-cost boundary for each intended application.
Whether any material has achieved the complete combination, including developments through November 1, 2026; the supplied freshness record cannot resolve this.
Full descriptions of the related concepts are needed to confirm overlaps beyond the distinctions inferable from their supplied titles.
